scenarios.name: backoff-doubles-to-the-cap
scenarios.description: The wait after the nth consecutive failure of a repository: the interval, doubled with each failure, capped at the smaller of 10 minutes and 10 times the interval.

scenarios.name: branch-segment-encode
scenarios.description: A branch name as one URL path segment: `/` becomes %2F, non-ASCII is percent-encoded; names git cannot use (empty, `..`, leading `-`, control characters, `@{`, lock suffix, a `%` ...) and names over 255 bytes are refused (the PR is then observed without the base tip read).

scenarios.name: branch-segment-guard
scenarios.description: The raw path segment the transport accepts for a branch: only what EncodeBranchSegment produces (an uppercase %2F, percent-encoded UTF-8); double encoding, dot segments, control characters, a literal slash and lowercase escapes are refused.

scenarios.name: checks-classify-classes
scenarios.description: The check class and the total of a head from its check runs and commit statuses (none, green, pending, red; skipped and neutral count green; a failure wins over pending).

scenarios.name: checks-classify-failing-names
scenarios.description: The failing names are sorted, at most 20, and counted in full.

scenarios.name: checks-debounce-and-epochs
scenarios.description: Check classes need two consecutive sightings; every accepted class change (also pending) bumps the checks epoch.

scenarios.name: checks-none-never-green
scenarios.description: An empty check list (class none) never produces checks-green; an accepted pending emits nothing.

scenarios.name: checks-not-read-keeps-class
scenarios.description: A cycle that did not read checks leaves the accepted class alone.

scenarios.name: checks-red-shape-stack
scenarios.description: A red head on a stacked base with the stack message has shape stack-merge-shape.

scenarios.name: checks-shape-rules
scenarios.description: The failure shape of a red head: real, stack-merge-shape or unknown, by the ordered rules (real markers first, stack patterns only on a stacked base and only if every failure is a plain failure with a pattern).

scenarios.name: checks-shape-text-bound
scenarios.description: Only the first 4 KiB of the summary and of the text count for the shape.

scenarios.name: closed-reopened-closed-generations
scenarios.description: A closed PR that reopens gets the next generation; closed and new-pr ids carry it.

scenarios.name: closed-replay-pins-generation
scenarios.description: The replay records the generation of a closed line so a later reopen gets generation 2.

scenarios.name: commit-list-decode
scenarios.description: The page of pulls/N/commits as the restacker reads it: the 40-hex SHAs in order, `more` when the page holds 100 items, a malformed body or a malformed transport error as `malformed`, any other transport error as `other`; the page is read unconditionally (no validator).

scenarios.name: corrupt-state-is-an-error-unless-baseline
scenarios.description: A corrupt state is an error when opening, never silently reset; a forced baseline repairs it.

scenarios.name: crash-after-append-before-print
scenarios.description: A crash after the journal append and before the print: nothing was printed; the start prints the event once.

scenarios.name: crash-base-changed-flapped-append1
scenarios.description: Replay effects, kind base-changed: the process dies after durable step append 1 of the cycle that emits it; the restart polls and sees the flapped observation. The journal holds the event exactly once and equals the crash-free run (crash-base-changed-flapped-none).

scenarios.name: default-state-dir
scenarios.description: The default state directory from the environment. Format-dependent (F3).

scenarios.name: event-id-counter
scenarios.description: How Go reads a counter (epoch, episode, generation) back from an event id when it rebuilds a lost state: the colon-separated part made of one letter and 1 to 8 digits, never a hex SHA. Format-dependent.

scenarios.name: event-id-keys
scenarios.description: How Go builds the event id (repo#pr:kind:key and the key of every kind). Format-dependent: a Rust port may use other ids as long as they are unique and stable per transition; the scenarios assert uniqueness, not these strings.

scenarios.name: event-json-shapes
scenarios.description: The JSON object of an event as Go writes it (every kind, no key omitted, lists never null) and the objects Go refuses to decode (unknown key, unknown kind, wrong schema version). The lines are format-dependent in key order and escaping; the key sets per kind and the refusals are the contract.

scenarios.name: first-run-silent-baseline
scenarios.description: The first successful read is a silent baseline; the next cycle announces only the change.

scenarios.name: flap-back-after-crash-next-epoch
scenarios.description: A flap back after a crash is a new event with the next epoch and nothing is lost.

scenarios.name: forced-baseline-after-state
scenarios.description: A forced baseline after a state exists is silent and replaces the accepted view; counters survive so ids stay unique.

scenarios.name: fork-flag-travels-in-new-pr-and-replay
scenarios.description: The fork flag travels in the new-pr event and is restored by the replay after a crash.

scenarios.name: generated-sequence-seed-01
scenarios.description: Generated forge sequence (seed 1, 14 cycles, two repositories, failures, merges, closes, reopens, unreadable merges and repository set changes) without a crash. The Go property test shows that the same sequence with random crashes yields the same journal.

scenarios.name: gone-unreadable-retried
scenarios.description: A PR that left the list with an unreadable pulls/N is retried every cycle and never guessed.

scenarios.name: head-change-resets-checks-and-candidates
scenarios.description: A head change clears the class and the stored candidates.

scenarios.name: head-changed-every-force-push
scenarios.description: head-changed fires on every force push including a return to an earlier head; every transition is a distinct event.

scenarios.name: http-conditional-round-trip
scenarios.description: A GET with and without a validator: a 200 carries ETag, body and the rate-limit headers, a request without a validator sends no If-None-Match; a 304 is a typed result (not an error) with no body; the accounting counts 2 requests and 1 not modified.

scenarios.name: http-error-classification
scenarios.description: HTTP status and body to error code: 401 unauthorized; 403 forbidden (404 too, with its status kept); a 403 with rate-limit evidence (remaining 0, Retry-After, or the secondary-limit text) and 429 rate-limited; 5xx http-5xx; any other success status and a body over 1 MiB malformed. The error text never carries the response body or a token and is bounded.

scenarios.name: http-negative-remaining-is-no-rate-limit-evidence
scenarios.description: A 403 whose only rate evidence is a negative remaining is forbidden, not rate-limited.

scenarios.name: http-not-modified-keeps-the-sent-validator
scenarios.description: A 304 returns the validator that was sent, weak prefix included, even if the server repeats another form.

scenarios.name: http-rate-limited-carries-reset-and-retry-after
scenarios.description: A rate-limited error carries the Retry-After seconds and the reset time from the headers.

scenarios.name: http-redirects-refused-and-repo-moved
scenarios.description: A 301 is never followed: repo-moved, with the new owner/name from the Location only if it names the repository safely (a hostile name, another host, an id URL or no Location give no name); any other redirect is malformed; the body of the redirect never leaks.

scenarios.name: http-token-never-in-errors
scenarios.description: A server that echoes the Authorization header in an error body does not make the token reachable from the error.

scenarios.name: http-typed-functions-and-refused-inputs
scenarios.description: Every typed read (list page, pulls/N, its commits, branch tip with an encoded name, commit, check runs, statuses, rate_limit) sends exactly its allowlisted GET; invalid inputs (bad repo names, number 0, a header-injecting validator, page and page-size bounds, a raw or dot branch name, a non-SHA commit) are refused before any request.

scenarios.name: http-unsolicited-304-is-malformed
scenarios.description: A 304 without a validator in the request is a malformed response.

scenarios.name: human-lines-golden
scenarios.description: The `--human` line of every kind: HH:MM:SS (UTC), repo#pr, kind, a summary; SHAs shortened to 7 characters. The restack-needed line carries Go's git command (owner decision F1: kept as in Go).

scenarios.name: human-lines-untrusted-text
scenarios.description: Text from the forge in a `--human` line never carries raw control characters, bidi or line separators, and a line is one line and bounded. The exact escaping is Go's (`untrusted.Esc`); the Rust port escapes differently (deviation D6), so only the properties are the contract.

scenarios.name: ignored-authors-and-labels
scenarios.description: Ignored authors and labels produce no events; a PR that becomes ignored vanishes silently.

scenarios.name: link-header-next-page
scenarios.description: The page number of the `rel="next"` entry of a Link header (rel with or without quotes); missing, malformed, zero and overflowing numbers give nothing.

scenarios.name: lost-state-keeps-counters-of-unconfigured-repos
scenarios.description: A lost state keeps the epoch counters of repositories that are no longer configured; they return with the next epoch.

scenarios.name: lost-state-rebuild-raises-checks-epoch
scenarios.description: A lost state rebuild raises the checks epoch of a baseline PR from the journal so later ids stay unique.

scenarios.name: lost-state-rebuilds-counters
scenarios.description: A lost state rebuilds the epoch counters from the journal so a later head-changed gets the next epoch; the old journal is not reprinted.

scenarios.name: lost-state-replay-timeout-at-higher-epoch
scenarios.description: The replay of a lost state restores the checks epoch and the fired flag of a timeout journalled at epoch 2.

scenarios.name: lost-state-silent-baseline-seq-gapless
scenarios.description: A lost state with a non-empty journal is a silent baseline and the journal continues without a gap.

scenarios.name: merge-marks-open-prs-detail-due
scenarios.description: A merge marks the other open PRs due for a detail read; a detail observation clears the mark.

scenarios.name: mergeable-behind-enters-and-leaves
scenarios.description: Entering and leaving behind is a mergeable-changed; a change of the state text alone is silent.

scenarios.name: mergeable-debounced-null-keeps
scenarios.description: mergeable-changed needs two sightings; a null mergeable keeps the previous value; a flap back is silent.

scenarios.name: merged-and-restack-needed
scenarios.description: A merge emits merged, then restack-needed for the children in ascending PR order; restack_due is cleared at the end of the cycle.

scenarios.name: merged-records-head-fork
scenarios.description: The merge records whether the merged PR's head lives in a fork: false only if the PR was observed open with its head in the base repository; a fork-merged or unobserved PR never yields class-1 candidates.

scenarios.name: merged-unreadable-commit
scenarios.description: A merge whose commit is unreadable has the key unknown and a null new parent.

scenarios.name: new-pr-details
scenarios.description: The details of new-pr and its time.

scenarios.name: null-mergeable-keeps-detail-due
scenarios.description: A confirming read that finds mergeability still being computed keeps the detail read due until a non-null read resolves the candidate.

scenarios.name: observe-baseline-reads-every-pr-fully
scenarios.description: The first observation of a repository reads every PR fully: list, pulls/N, branch tips, check runs and commit statuses; a null mergeable is `not computed`; the fork flag comes from pulls/N; check data keeps title, summary and text; a status context is taken once (the newest).

scenarios.name: observe-confirms-a-debounce-candidate
scenarios.description: A class that changed upstream is reported; the stored candidate (accepted class still differs) makes the next read fresh, not conditional, so the second sighting reaches the core; once the core accepted the class the PR is settled and not read.

scenarios.name: observe-confirms-a-stored-candidate-in-a-new-process
scenarios.description: A candidate stored by the core survives a restart: the memory of the observer is gone, so the known PR itself (class candidate) makes a fresh read due.

scenarios.name: observe-default-branch-guess
scenarios.description: The default branch is guessed from the bases of the open PRs (main, then master; stacked bases and unknown names give nothing); the allowlist has no repository read.

scenarios.name: observe-detail-after-a-merge-in-the-same-cycle
scenarios.description: When a known PR left the open list and pulls/N says merged, every open PR is re-read; the merged PR is reported as gone with merge commit, head, base, merged_at and method hint (one parent: rebase-or-squash).

scenarios.name: observe-detail-due-flag-and-slow-refresh
scenarios.description: A PR marked due gets a fresh read; every detail_every cycles the PR numbered so that (cycle + number) mod 10 = 0 gets a conditional refresh (staggered by number).

scenarios.name: observe-detail-when-base-tip-moved
scenarios.description: A moved base tip (the only evidence that the base moved) makes the PRs on that base due for a fresh, unconditional pulls/N read; PRs on other bases are not read.

scenarios.name: observe-detail-when-head-changed
scenarios.description: A PR whose head changed gets a fresh pulls/N read and its checks read; the other PRs are left alone.

scenarios.name: observe-fork-flag-only-when-detail-was-read
scenarios.description: The fork flag is reported as an answer (fork_known) only when pulls/N was read with a body in this observation; an unread or 304-answered detail reports no answer.

scenarios.name: observe-gone-closed-merged-and-still-open
scenarios.description: A PR that left the list is read once via pulls/N: closed (no merge), merged with two parents (merge), merged with an unreadable commit (null commit, unknown), still open (stays unresolved); an unreadable commit only makes the hint unknown; an unreadable pulls/N fails the repository.

scenarios.name: observe-keeps-watching-when-a-base-name-is-refused
scenarios.description: A base branch name that cannot be encoded for a URL is skipped with one diagnostic per run; the PRs on it are still observed.

scenarios.name: observe-maps-failures-and-the-rate-limit
scenarios.description: Read failures map to watch-error codes; a rate limit below 10 percent asks for a slower interval; below 50 remaining arms a hold that the next Observe reports once as a run-wide rate-limited error (wait until reset + 5 s); a canceled run is not a repository failure.

scenarios.name: observe-refuses-invalid-values-of-a-gone-pr
scenarios.description: pulls/N of a PR that left the list is validated: a merge commit with an escape or in uppercase, a short head, an unparsable or missing merged_at, a closed PR with a bad head are malformed responses.

scenarios.name: observe-skips-ignored-prs
scenarios.description: Ignored PRs (author or label) stay in the list for the core but cost no detail and no checks read.

scenarios.name: observe-steady-state-reads-only-the-basics
scenarios.description: In the steady state (all PRs accepted green, no due flag, no moved base) a cycle reads the list and one conditional branch tip per base; no detail, no checks, nothing reported for PRs.

scenarios.name: partial-batch-crash-after-append-1
scenarios.description: A crash after journal append 1 of 4 leaves a partial batch; the poll after the restart completes the rest in the order of the crash-free run.

scenarios.name: partial-batch-crash-after-append-2
scenarios.description: A crash after journal append 2 of 4 leaves a partial batch; the poll after the restart completes the rest in the order of the crash-free run.

scenarios.name: partial-batch-crash-after-append-3
scenarios.description: A crash after journal append 3 of 4 leaves a partial batch; the poll after the restart completes the rest in the order of the crash-free run.

scenarios.name: partial-batch-crash-free
scenarios.description: Four events in one cycle without a crash (the reference of the partial batch scenarios).

scenarios.name: pending-timeout-disabled-with-zero
scenarios.description: A pending timeout of 0 disables checks-pending-timeout.

scenarios.name: pending-timeout-once-per-period
scenarios.description: checks-pending-timeout fires once per pending period (limit 10 minutes) and again after a class change.

scenarios.name: pulls-304-reuses-stored-link-and-items
scenarios.description: With the stored state every page is requested conditionally; all 304 means unchanged with the stored items; the Link chain comes from the stored Link because GitHub's 304 has none; a changed middle page is replaced while the others stay 304.

scenarios.name: pulls-errors-pass-through
scenarios.description: A 301 on the list is repo-moved with the new name; a rate-limited list is not retried.

scenarios.name: pulls-halved-page-size-is-in-memory-only
scenarios.description: The halved page size lives in the reader until restart (per repository); it is not read from the stored state: a new reader with the stored 12-sized state starts at 25 without validators.

scenarios.name: pulls-halves-page-size-and-restarts-at-page-one
scenarios.description: A page over 1 MiB halves the page size to 12 and restarts at page 1; 12 is kept for the repository (conditional requests at 12 afterwards).

scenarios.name: pulls-no-probe-beyond-the-allowlist-bound
scenarios.description: At the page bound (80 full pages) a 304 listing does not probe a page beyond the allowlist: 80 requests.

scenarios.name: pulls-page-too-large-at-twelve
scenarios.description: A page over 1 MiB at 12 per page (by body or by declared length) is page-too-large after exactly two requests.

scenarios.name: pulls-page-too-large-by-declared-length
scenarios.description: The declared Content-Length alone over 1 MiB gives page-too-large too.

scenarios.name: pulls-paginate-with-link-across-three-pages
scenarios.description: The open list is read page by page by the Link rel=next header (25 per page, the next page must be exactly the current plus one); the items are parsed to number, title, user, labels, draft, head sha and ref, base ref and sha; each page's ETag and Link are kept.

scenarios.name: pulls-probes-past-a-full-last-page-on-304
scenarios.description: A 304 reuses the stored Link, so an exactly full last page could hide a reopened PR behind it: the next page is probed once (first time unconditionally, then conditionally); a 200 is authoritative and needs no probe; a short last page is never probed.

scenarios.name: pulls-rejects-bad-bounds-links-and-items
scenarios.description: max_open_prs outside 1..2000 is refused without a request; a Link that skips a page, goes backwards or has no number is never followed (malformed); malformed list bodies (not an array, number 0, short sha, non-objects, not JSON) are malformed.

scenarios.name: pulls-short-last-page-is-not-probed
scenarios.description: A short last page (24 of 25) is never probed on a 304.

scenarios.name: pulls-too-many-open-prs-12-per-page-max-2000
scenarios.description: An endless list at 12 per page with max_open_prs 2000 stops with too-many-open-prs after exactly 167 pages.

scenarios.name: pulls-too-many-open-prs-25-per-page-max-2000
scenarios.description: An endless list at 25 per page with max_open_prs 2000 stops with too-many-open-prs after exactly 80 pages.

scenarios.name: pulls-too-many-open-prs-25-per-page-max-25
scenarios.description: An endless list at 25 per page with max_open_prs 25 stops with too-many-open-prs after exactly 1 pages.

scenarios.name: pulls-too-many-open-prs-25-per-page-max-30
scenarios.description: An endless list at 25 per page with max_open_prs 30 stops with too-many-open-prs after exactly 2 pages.

scenarios.name: pulls-too-many-open-prs-on-the-last-page
scenarios.description: More items than max_open_prs on the last page is too-many-open-prs.

scenarios.name: rate-limit-assess
scenarios.description: The slowdown policy: none; slow (remaining below 10 percent of the limit: double the interval); wait (remaining below 50 or exhausted: wait until reset + 5 s).

scenarios.name: rate-limit-headers
scenarios.description: The X-RateLimit-* headers: a negative remaining is not evidence (unknown); zero remaining is.

scenarios.name: rate-limited-wait-until
scenarios.description: Until when a rate-limited answer holds the run: retry-after plus 5 s, else reset plus 5 s (only if in the future), else 65 s from now.

scenarios.name: ready-state-and-base-changed
scenarios.description: ready-state-changed and base-changed are immediate.

scenarios.name: reopened-pr-keeps-counters
scenarios.description: A reopened PR keeps its epoch counters so event ids stay unique.

scenarios.name: repos-changed-added-removed-abab
scenarios.description: A repository added gets a silent baseline; every change of the repository set is a distinct repos-changed (ABAB).

scenarios.name: repos-changed-skipped-submodule
scenarios.description: A skipped submodule is reported once in repos-changed.

scenarios.name: repository-in-backoff-not-polled
scenarios.description: A repository in backoff is not polled; recovery comes with the first successful poll after it.

scenarios.name: restack-candidates
scenarios.description: Which open PRs must be restacked after a merge: class 1 child-of-merged-branch by the base name alone, class 2 contains-merged-commits by the old parent in the commit list (at most 3 pages), ascending by PR number. The `argv` of a candidate is Go's fixed git command; it is null for a fork head or an unknown merge commit (owner decision F1: kept as in Go, an exception to D-20261103-03).

scenarios.name: restack-hosting-name-check
scenarios.description: The restacker of `stw watch` refuses a head branch that the hosting reader cannot put into a URL segment (a percent sign, for example) with a diagnostic, and goes on with the others.

scenarios.name: retry-after-header
scenarios.description: The Retry-After header in seconds: 0 to 86400 accepted, anything else (negative, over a day, garbage, empty) is no evidence.

scenarios.name: run-human-output-and-slowdown
scenarios.description: `--human` prints the human line; a rate limit below 10 percent doubles the wait between polls.

scenarios.name: run-interrupted-until-event-is-a-failure
scenarios.description: An interrupted `--until-event` exits 1 (interrupted) and never looks like a match.

scenarios.name: run-once-baseline-then-transitions
scenarios.description: `--once`: the first run is a silent baseline (exit 0, no output); the next prints only the transition; `--baseline` after a state exists prints nothing and replaces the state.

scenarios.name: run-once-fails-only-when-no-repository-could-be-read
scenarios.description: `--once` exits 1 only when no repository could be read at all; the failure is still data on stdout (a watch-error event); a readable repository exits 0.

scenarios.name: run-rate-limit-holds-the-whole-run
scenarios.description: An exhausted rate limit holds the whole run until the reset: one run-level watch-error rate-limited (repo null) and a sleep of at least 9 minutes.

scenarios.name: run-restack-needed-end-to-end
scenarios.description: A merge read through the observer produces restack-needed for the child on the merged branch (class 1) and for the PR whose commits contain the old head (class 2), not for the unrelated PR; the event carries old parent, new parent, merged PR and Go's argv (owner decision F1).

scenarios.name: run-status-fresh-stale-missing
scenarios.description: `--status`: fresh within the window (exit 0), stale (exit 5, JSON fresh=false), missing heartbeat (exit 5), a relative directory (exit 2).

scenarios.name: run-stream-ends-on-interrupt
scenarios.description: A `--stream` interrupted (SIGINT/SIGTERM) ends with exit 0.

scenarios.name: run-stream-ends-on-max-idle
scenarios.description: A `--stream` with `--max-idle 150s` and no event ends with exit 0 after exactly 150 s of sleeping.

scenarios.name: run-until-event-matches-a-kind
scenarios.description: `--until-event`: exits 0 as soon as a poll printed an event of a requested kind; the wait between polls is the interval.

scenarios.name: run-until-event-prints-the-whole-poll
scenarios.description: `--until-event` matching a kind still prints every event of that poll before it exits.

scenarios.name: run-until-event-timeout-exits-four
scenarios.description: `--until-event` without a matching event ends exactly at the timeout with exit 4 and no output; the last sleep is shortened to the remaining time.

scenarios.name: run-usage-and-failure-exit-codes
scenarios.description: Exit codes before any read: a relative state directory and a state directory inside a Git work tree are usage errors (2, nothing created); a state directory with a wide mode, a reader that cannot open (no token: `hosting-api-unavailable`, before any request) and a corrupt state (never silently reset, the message names --baseline) are failures (1); `--baseline` repairs the corrupt state.

scenarios.name: run-wide-rate-limit-holds-the-poll
scenarios.description: A run-wide failure (rate-limited) holds the whole poll, is reported without a repo, and recovers without one.

scenarios.name: second-merge-same-child-distinct-ids
scenarios.description: A second merge for the same child is a distinct restack-needed transition.

scenarios.name: status-fresh-stale-after-a-failing-cycle
scenarios.description: The heartbeat freshness window (3 minutes at a 60 s interval) and the per-repository status after a failing cycle.

scenarios.name: status-freshness-window
scenarios.description: How old the heartbeat may be for `--status` to report fresh: the larger of 3 intervals and 3 minutes.

scenarios.name: stdout-twice-when-crash-follows-print
scenarios.description: A crash after the print leaves the event on stdout twice (at-least-once); the journal holds it once and a completed cycle prints nothing more.

scenarios.name: stored-candidates-visible-in-hints
scenarios.description: A stored class candidate and a stored mergeability candidate show in the hints for the observer (detail read due).

scenarios.name: timeout-no-refire-after-forced-baseline
scenarios.description: A pending timeout that already fired is not fired again after a forced baseline.

scenarios.name: timeout-no-refire-after-lost-state
scenarios.description: A pending timeout that already fired is not fired again after a lost state.

scenarios.name: timeout-no-refire-after-repo-remove-readd
scenarios.description: A pending timeout that already fired is not fired again after the repository was removed and added again.

scenarios.name: unknown-fork-never-overwrites-persisted
scenarios.description: A fork flag read without pulls/N is not an answer: it never overwrites a persisted fork flag, also not through a baseline.

scenarios.name: watch-config-parse
scenarios.description: The strict profile of `.stw/watch.toml`: every key read; unknown keys and tables, wrong types, duplicate keys, a missing or different schema_version, bad repo names, out-of-range numbers and invalid TOML are errors (usage, exit 2).

scenarios.name: watch-decode-pull-detail
scenarios.description: The fields read from pulls/N: mergeable (null = not computed), mergeable_state, rebaseable, head sha, and the fork flag (head repository missing or different from the base repository, case-insensitive); a body that is not an object is malformed.

scenarios.name: watch-endpoint-allowlist
scenarios.description: The GET endpoints the watch reader may call (pulls list with page bounds 80 at 25 and 167 at 12, pulls/N, its commits up to page 3, branches with an encoded segment, commits/SHA with check-runs and statuses, rate_limit) and what it refuses. Only GET exists (the Go guard refuses every write method on every endpoint; Rust must have no write path).

scenarios.name: watch-error-episodes
scenarios.description: watch-error per episode and code; a long outage also stalls; recovery closes the episode; a second episode gets a new id.

scenarios.name: watch-error-every-tenth-failure
scenarios.description: watch-error repeats at the 1st, 10th and 20th failure of an episode.

scenarios.name: watch-error-message-sanitized-and-bounded
scenarios.description: The error message is sanitized (no control characters) and bounded to 512 bytes.

scenarios.name: watch-parse-remote
scenarios.description: OWNER/NAME of a remote URL for a host (https, ssh://, scp-like; .git and a trailing slash removed; a local path, another host, extra path segments and `..` refused).

scenarios.name: watch-prepare-flags
scenarios.description: The validated run of `stw watch` from its flags (and a config file given as text): defaults (stream, 60 s, detail every 10, pending timeout 45 min, 2000 open PRs), `--until-event` (timeout 590 s), the flags that exclude each other and every usage error (exit 2: nothing read, nothing written), the config merge (flags win), and the state directory of `--status`.

scenarios.name: watch-resolve-repositories
scenarios.description: The repository set of a run: --repo flags, then the workspace members with a GitHub remote on the host, then the config repos, in this order, without duplicates (case-insensitive); everything else in the workspace is skipped and reported with a reason; no source, a bad name, a failing discovery, a workspace without a GitHub repository and more than 256 repositories are usage errors.

scenarios.name: watch-split-remote
scenarios.description: Host and path of a remote URL without judging either; a local path or an unsupported scheme is refused.

scenarios.name: watch-stalled-once-both-episodes-recover
scenarios.description: watch-stalled fires once per stall; recovery emits watch-recovered for the error episode first, then the stall.

scenarios.name: watch-valid-host
scenarios.description: A host name with an optional port for `--host`.

scenarios.name: workspace-id
scenarios.description: The state directory id: the first 16 hex digits of SHA-256 over host and workspace root or the sorted, de-duplicated, lowercased repository list. Format-dependent (F3: a Rust port may use another id).
